biography.plain_text: Francesco Merloni (1925–2024) was an Italian industrialist, engineer and politician who developed the family heating division into Ariston Group, an international manufacturer of water-heating and thermal-comfort systems. He led the business for more than four decades, served seven terms in parliament and was Italy's Minister of Public Works under two governments.
biography.html: Francesco Merloni (1925–2024) was an Italian industrialist, engineer and politician who developed the family heating division into Ariston Group, an international manufacturer of water-heating and thermal-comfort systems. He led the business for more than four decades, served seven terms in parliament and was Italy's Minister of Public Works under two governments.

long_biography.plain_text:
While studying industrial engineering, Merloni designed a welded-cylinder factory for the business founded by his father, Aristide. He joined the company in the 1950s and expanded cylinder production before moving into water heaters. After Aristide's death, Francesco took charge of the heating and plumbing division, broadening it into boilers, heat pumps and international manufacturing through new plants and acquisitions.

Business was only one part of his public life. Merloni sat in the Italian parliament across seven legislatures and served as Minister of Public Works under the Amato and Ciampi governments, where a major public-procurement reform carried his name. He later handed executive leadership of Ariston to the next generation and became honorary chairman, remaining associated with Fabriano's industrial and civic development until his death at 99.
